standard_prerequisites.name: Half adjoint equivalence
standard_prerequisites.statement: ishae(f) consists of g, eta : g o f ~ id, epsilon : f o g ~ id and the coherence tau : prd x, f(eta x) = epsilon(f x).
standard_prerequisites.use: Its four components are the data used throughout the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Paths in a fiber
standard_prerequisites.statement: (x,p) = (x',p') in the fiber of f at y is equivalent to Sigma gamma : x = x', ap f gamma `ct` p' = p.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the retained characterisation applied at source line 272.

standard_prerequisites.name: Naturality of epsilon
standard_prerequisites.statement: The homotopy epsilon satisfies its naturality identity on paths.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the last equality of the displayed chain at source line 280.

core_obligations: Unpack the hypothesis as (g, eta, epsilon, tau) : ishae(f) and fix y : B (source line 269).
Choose (g y, epsilon y) as the centre of contraction of the fiber (source line 270).
For an arbitrary (x,p) in the fiber, reduce by the retained path characterisation to producing gamma : g y = x with ap f gamma `ct` p = epsilon y (source lines 271-272).

Set gamma := opp(g p) `ct` eta x and compute the three-step chain: ap f of that composite, then the substitution f(eta x) = epsilon(f x) by tau x, and finally the naturality of epsilon, which yields epsilon y (source lines 273-280).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack the half adjoint equivalence and choose the centre.
Reduce to a path in A and define gamma.
Verify the required identity by the displayed chain.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled theorem `thm:contr-hae` at source lines 265-267: if f is a half adjoint equivalence then every fiber of f is contractible. The author's proof (source lines 268-281) is an explicit contraction: it unpacks the four components of ishae(f) and names (g y, epsilon y) as the centre (lines 269-270), then reduces the comparison with an arbitrary fiber element to a path in the source via the retained characterisation of paths in a fiber (lines 271-272), and defines gamma := opp(g p) `ct` eta x so that the required identity ap f gamma `ct` p = epsilon y holds by a three-step computation in which tau x is used for the middle step and naturality of epsilon for the last one (lines 273-280). The statement records only the contractibility, not the choice of centre or the explicit path that realizes it.
